body.p: You can create custom project templates and attach them to a custom framework. This makes them available in the New Project wizard so users can create projects from a predefined structure.

Project templates are stored in the templates directory inside a framework. In addition to the archive-based .zxpr format, also supports directory-based project templates that use a .dxpr folder. The directory-based format is useful when developing or maintaining templates because you can edit the files directly without repackaging an archive.

To create a project template, follow these steps:
Create the project structure that you want to use as a starting point for new projects. The template content should include the project .xpr file and any other resources that need to be copied when the project is created.
Save the template in the templates directory of your framework by using one of the following formats:
Archive-based format - Create a ZIP archive with a .zxpr extension. The archive should contain the .xpr file at the first level, along with the other resources used by the template.
Directory-based format - Create a folder whose name ends with .dxpr. Place the .xpr file and the other template resources directly inside that folder.
Create or edit the sibling .properties file for the template to configure how it is displayed in the New Project wizard. The properties file should have the same base name as the template. For example, use Sample Project.properties for either Sample Project.zxpr or Sample Project.dxpr.
If needed, add properties such as displayName or description to control the label and description shown in the wizard. You can also configure icons in the same way as for document templates. For details, see Customizing Document Templates.
Test the template by opening the New Project wizard and selecting your template.
body.note: For both .zxpr archives and .dxpr folders, the template content should not be wrapped in an extra top-level folder. The project .xpr file and the other resources should be placed directly at the first level of the template.
body.p: When a user creates a project from a template, copies the template resources into the selected project directory. The proposed project file name is determined from the .xpr file inside the template. If no .xpr file is found, the template name is used.
